title: Each supported target integration profile names its own probe path, response contract, transport, and semantic distinction
description: Every profile the blueprint ships names four things: the probe path or command surface (an HTTP path for HTTP profiles, a TCP port for socket profiles, a shell command for exec profiles, a supervisor call for notify profiles); the response contract (HTTP status code range with an optional minimal JSON body for HTTP profiles, connect-and-close for TCP, exit-code zero for exec, one notify call for supervisor); the transport (HTTP GET, TCP SYN, spawned process, or unix socket for supervisor calls); and the semantic distinction between liveness and readiness (two endpoints for Kubernetes; one health signal for load balancers and uptime monitors that do not distinguish; a boot-time readiness notification followed by a periodic watchdog for systemd; a single command answer for Docker HEALTHCHECK). A profile that does not resolve all four is refused at boot with a stable-coded error naming the missing field.
rationale: The five properties are the elicitation shape. Different external supervisors answer differently on each of them, and the differences are load-bearing: a load balancer that only reads HTTP status has no use for a JSON body; a Kubernetes TCPSocket probe never touches an HTTP path; a systemd unit under Type=notify blocks on a boot notification and then expects periodic watchdog pings, not a synchronous probe. Naming the four properties explicitly per profile is what the elicitation surface exists to do.
